title: Ka'b ibn Malik
hook: one of the three who stayed behind from Tabuk and refused to lie (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Hassan ibn Thabit, who answered the Prophet's critics in verse. Your line was the poet's pulpit.

The army has come home, and one by one, the men who stayed behind file in to explain themselves. Each has a reason, and swears to it. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, listens, accepts what they say, and asks God to forgive them. Then it's Ka'b's turn. He's a good talker, and he knows it. He could build an excuse in his sleep. And he has no excuse at all. He simply put off getting ready, day after day, until the army was gone. Today: Ka'b ibn Malik, and the story he tells against himself.
screen: `THE MEN WHO STAYED BEHIND.` → `ONE EXCUSE AFTER ANOTHER.` → `KA'B HAS NONE.`

segments.voice: Ka'b tells it himself, in a long report in Sahih al-Bukhari. Before the Tabuk expedition, he says, he had never been stronger or better off. He kept meaning to prepare, and kept not doing it. Then the army left. When the Prophet returned, Ka'b came before him, and the Prophet smiled the smile of someone who is angry. If I lie to you today, he told the Prophet, you may be pleased with me now, and God will soon turn you against me. If I tell you the truth, you'll be angry, and I hope for God's forgiveness. I had no excuse. The Prophet said: as for this one, he has told the truth. Go, until God decides about you. Then the hard part. People were told not to speak to Ka'b and the two others who had owned up. He would greet the Prophet and wonder whether his lips moved to answer. His own cousin would not reply to him. A letter came from a foreign king inviting him over, and Ka'b threw it in the oven. Fifty nights, the report says, the earth felt narrow to him. Then the Qur'an spoke, in surah nine, of the three who were left behind, and of God turning to them in mercy. A man climbed a hill and shouted the good news. Ka'b's conclusion is the line he chose to be remembered by: God saved me only through truthfulness, and part of my repentance is to speak nothing but the truth as long as I live. Not quickly. Not comfortably. But truth saved him.
screen: `I HAD NO EXCUSE.` · `AS FOR THIS ONE, HE HAS TOLD THE TRUTH.` · `NO ONE WOULD SPEAK TO HIM.` · `GOD TURNED TO THE THREE.` · then, large: `TRUTH SAVED HIM.`

segments.voice: Look for one thing you've been explaining away: a late reply with a made-up reason, a mistake you let someone else carry, a small cover story. Say to yourself, plainly, what actually happened, with no excuse attached, and notice how that sits. If you pray, you can ask God for the courage of Ka'b.
Ka'b, the companion who had no excuse for missing Tabuk, told the truth instead of lying his way out, and was forgiven through the Qur'an. Today's word.
Your line: truth saved him. Fifty narrow nights, and then mercy. Day eight hundred fifty-two, done.

howItsDone: Muslims tell Ka'b ibn Malik's story from his own long account in Sahih al-Bukhari, read alongside surah 9:118, as a lesson in truthfulness and repentance.

fork.setup: you are Ka'b. you missed the expedition with no excuse, and you're good with words. the Prophet is waiting. what do you say?
options: make up a good excuse, like the others.
tell him plainly: I had no excuse.
fork.reveal: Bukhari keeps his words: if I lie you may be pleased now, and God will turn you against me. I had no excuse. it cost him dearly, and it saved him.

chat.says: Why did Ka'b admit he had no excuse, when the others got off easily?
options: He chose the truth over a lie that would only please people for now.
He was too proud to make excuses, so he took the punishment instead.
He hoped an honest answer would get him a lighter punishment.
chat.meaning: In Bukhari, Ka'b says: if I lie you may be pleased now; if I tell the truth I hope for God's forgiveness. Truthfulness saved him.
